title: repos-connections
description: Which repositories are related to which, and how. A generator sweeps each participating repository for a declaration of the endpoints it serves and the endpoints it calls, matches the two, and writes the result here. agentmemory reads it to decide which related repositories' memory is relevant to a session in any one of them. This schema constrains the shape and nothing else: it names no generator, no declaration format, and no repository, so any producer emitting this shape works.

schema_version.description: Bumped when a change to this schema breaks a reader. A consumer that does not recognise the value should stop rather than guess, because a silently misread graph names the wrong repositories.

manifest_path.description: Repository-relative path of the per-repository declaration the generator swept. Recorded so a reader can tell which producer wrote the file, and where to look when an entry seems wrong. Each producer chooses its own path.

repos.description: Every repository that published a declaration, sorted by `repo` so a rebuild diffs cleanly. A repository that published nothing is absent, and its absence is invisible here: nothing in this file can distinguish 'reaches no other repository' from 'never declared anything'. A consumer that needs that distinction has to compare against whatever registry lists the repositories it expects.

repo.description: Where the generator found this repository, which is authoritative over any identity the repository declares about itself. A declaration is written once and goes stale when a repository moves between organisations.

service.description: The label this repository's endpoints are namespaced under. Deliberately not globally unique; `repo` is what disambiguates two repositories claiming the same label.

related.description: The other repositories this one reaches, sorted by repository then role. Empty where a repository declared endpoints that nothing else references.

relationship.description: One directed relationship, written from the perspective of the repository whose entry holds it. Every relationship appears twice in the file, once on each participant, so a reader holding one repository finds its related repositories without scanning the whole document.

repo.description: The repository at the other end. Never equal to the entry's own `repo`: a repository calling its own endpoint is not a cross-repository relationship.

role.description: The entry repository's own side. `provider` serves the endpoints listed; `consumer` calls them. The repository at the other end holds the opposite role for the same endpoints.

endpoints.description: The endpoint keys this relationship rests on, sorted and unique. These are the only thing joining two repositories whose code shares no import, which is the case this file exists for: a consumer that builds its URLs at runtime has no compile-time reference to its provider.

repoName.description: A repository as `owner/name`, the form the GitHub API and CODEOWNERS both use.

endpointKey.description: A service label and a path, separated by one space. The HTTP method is deliberately absent: a declaration may name a surface as a bare path where the repository serving it declares several verbs, and those are one surface. Keying on the verb would leave the bare reference orphaned beside the real entries, inventing an endpoint nobody serves.
